meta.title: Machiavelli: is it better to be feared or loved?
meta.search_phrase: better to be feared or loved machiavelli

plates.query: Santi di Tito portrait of Niccolò Machiavelli
Renaissance portrait of a prince in armour painting

beats.text: Machiavelli asked rulers a cold question: is it better to be feared, or to be loved?
Ideally, both. But sooner or later the two collide, and you must choose one.
Love, he warned, is a bond people break the moment it stops being convenient for them.
Fear holds, because it rests on something people never shake off — the dread of punishment.
"It is far safer to be feared than loved," he wrote, "if one of the two must be wanting."
But one rule above all: never be hated. A feared ruler survives; a hated one is torn down.
Cynical? Perhaps. Or simply the first man honest enough to describe power as it actually works.

source_note: Quote: The Prince, trans. W. K. Marriott (public domain).
